trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out to (4,1,6), to (6,2,7), to (7,2,6) or to (6,1,4) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (4,1,6).
Going to (2,1,6), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (4,2,7).
Going to (6,2,7) would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (2,2,7), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4,7). So the line goes to (4,4,7).
Going to (4,6,7) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (2,4,7).
The line must go to (2,2,7): to (1,4,6) is number 7, which comes later; to (2,6,7) is number 9, which comes later.
I can't rule out to (1,2,6) or to (2,1,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (1,2,6).
Cell (2,1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,1,4).
Going to (2,1,2), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (1,2,4).
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (2,1,2) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (1,4,2).
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (2,7,4) would force the line onto number 11 before its turn. So the line goes to (2,6,7).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,6,7).
Number 10 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (4,7,4): to (6,7,6) is number 13, which comes later.
Going to (6,7,4), the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4,1). So the line goes to (2,7,4).
Going to (2,7,2) would strand number 11: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (1,6,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,6,2).
Going to (2,6,1), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (2,7,2).
Going to (2,6,1), the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,6,1). So the line goes to (4,7,2).
The line must go to (6,7,2): to (4,6,1) is number 22, which comes later.
Going to (6,6,1) would leave number 13 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,7,4).
Number 13 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (6,6,7): to (7,6,6) is number 15, which comes later.
Cell (6,2,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,2,6).
Going to (7,2,4) would leave number 15 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,4,6).
Number 15 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (7,2,4) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (7,4,2).
Going to (6,4,1) would strand number 17: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (7,6,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,6,1).
Going to (6,2,1), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 18. So the line goes to (4,4,1).
Going to (2,4,1) would cut off a group of 2 cells. So the line goes to (4,2,1).
Going to (4,1,2) would leave both cell (2,1,2) and number 20 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,2,1).
Going to number 19, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (7,2,4). So the line goes to (6,1,2).

Going to (4,1,2) would leave both cell (2,1,2) and number 20 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going to (6,1,4) would leave both cell (7,2,4) and number 20 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (7,2,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,2,4).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
